title: 5th Sitting of First session of 2026
summary: The 5th sitting of the session opened at 10:30 on Sunday 8 March 2026, which was also International Women's Day, and the chair accepted the minutes of sittings 1 to 4. Four more non-resident ambassador nominations (Argentina, Cambodia and Vietnam, Greece, Bosnia and Herzegovina) went to the Foreign Relations Committee, and MPs continued debating the government's National Service Bill. The committee's reports on non-resident ambassadors to Serbia, Malta, Oman and Armenia were debated, with some MPs questioning embassy costs and the Middle East war, and each was approved 62-0 at the vote. The Employment Act amendment bill was also debated, and a proposal to lengthen mothers' childcare breaks from 30 to 45 minutes was rejected 7-49. The text was readable, but the leave count and some wording are uncertain because of dropped marks. This part covers the final stretch of the debate on the Employment Act (2008/2) amendment bill, which the government sponsored through the Madaveli member. A second amendment from the Thoddoo member would let the Cabinet exempt certain types of business from paying the employment quota fee, with exemptions starting from the following year. The House rejected that amendment 7-51, then passed the bill itself 62-0. The chair closed the sitting with Ramadan and Eid greetings. The presiding member is not named in this part, and the attendance figure (63 present of 93) comes from the vote tallies, not the attendance item.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Backed the National Service Bill and the committee reports on ambassadors, saying nominees are qualified and costs are being cut.
Presented the committee report on the Employment Act amendment bill and rebutted opposition criticism of how the committee worked.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Presented the Foreign Relations Committee reports on ambassadors to Serbia and Malta, Oman and Armenia, noting the nominees met the legal requirements.
Backed the National Service Bill as a way to give youth skills and responsibility.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Backed the Oman nominee but urged the government to prepare for price rises and tourism losses from the Middle East war.
Raised concern that the Employment Act changes cut public-holiday overtime and widen foreign worker quotas.
Seconded the amendment to extend childcare breaks.
Seconded the Thoddoo member's amendment.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Said the 2008 Employment Act was an MDP law, backed the amendments overall, and proposed a 45-minute childcare break instead of 30.
Said fees such as worker quotas should be set through parliament.
Proposed an amendment letting Cabinet exempt employers in certain business types from the quota fee, with each exemption taking effect from the next year with the state budget.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the Employment Act amendments, saying childcare time now runs two years and conditions improve.
Criticised MDP attendance and statements, and argued the government has put foreign worker matters in order.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the National Service Bill as training that prepares young people, especially girls, for work.
Supported the Employment Act amendments, saying the childcare break helps mothers and urging more day care centres.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Supported the Serbia and Malta report but questioned about 54 million rufiyaa a month spent on embassies and urged savings elsewhere.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Said the National Service Bill mainly serves uniformed service and government messaging, and that Maldivians should instead be trained to take tourism jobs now held by foreigners.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Backed the bill as a fix for youth skills gaps, citing large foreign shares in tourism, nursing and teaching, and asked for refinement at committee stage.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Supported the bill, saying school leavers need practical skills, and asked that the programme be widened to a year with loan and job support.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: On the Armenia report, said the foreign ministry's monthly budget rose from 23 to 54 million rufiyaa and asked what embassies deliver.

decisions: The minutes of sittings 1 to 4 were accepted without amendment.
Four non-resident ambassador nominations (Argentina, Cambodia and Vietnam, Greece, Bosnia and Herzegovina) were sent to the Foreign Relations Committee.
Parliament approved the non-resident ambassador appointments to Serbia, Malta, Oman and Armenia, each by 62 votes to 0.
An amendment to give mothers two 45-minute childcare breaks a day (instead of 30) in the Employment Act amendment bill was rejected, 7 yes to 49 no.
The sitting paused from 12:00 to 13:01 and the third reading of the Employment Act amendment bill was set for the vote hour.
Second amendment to the Employment Act (2008/2) amendment bill not passed, 7 for and 51 against.
Bill to amend the Employment Act (2008/2) passed by the People's Majlis, 62 for and 0 against.
Sitting closed by the chair with Ramadan and Eid greetings.
